_comment: The query mix the load test replays. Base questions are the eval golden set (eval/golden.json) so the workload is the same material the retrieval evaluation uses; the paraphrases are written by hand to be the same question in different words, which is what a semantic cache is supposed to catch. The topics are combined into questions nobody has asked, to stand for the share of any real workload a cache can do nothing about — they have to be genuinely different text, or the unique share is not unique and the hit rate is flattered.

passages: Deduplication uses a cosine distance threshold of 0.451, converted from the previously calibrated L2 value of 0.95.
The daemon owns the SQLite database and serializes every write through a single process, so concurrent writers cannot fight over it.
Hybrid retrieval runs a vector KNN and a BM25 keyword search, then fuses the two rankings with reciprocal rank fusion at k=60.
Reranking is off by default because it costs an extra local LLM call and has not yet been shown to help on this corpus.
Verification splits an answer into claims and tests each one against the retrieved passages, reporting a groundedness rate.
The context window is len(prompt)/3 plus headroom, clamped to between 4096 and 32768 tokens.
The database lives at ~/.engrex/engrex.db and the file watcher watches ~/Engrex for dropped files.
The HNSW benchmark reports build time, exact versus approximate query latency, speedup, recall and memory.
The browser extension posts captured page text to 127.0.0.1:7777/capture, which the daemon's HTTP server ingests.
RawText stubs are written into a subfolder that the watcher does not watch, so they are never re-ingested.
